EXP-001.did: We froze the shopping cart service for a few seconds, like switching off one cash register in a busy store.
EXP-001.expected: Cart pages would break, but the rest of the shop should survive.
EXP-001.happened: Cart pages froze and requests timed out. Our emergency brake stopped the test and restored the cart in 0.51 seconds.
EXP-001.means: The cart is a weak spot: if it fails, customers cannot check out. Fix: add a circuit breaker and degraded cart mode.

EXP-002.did: We froze the Redis datastore that saves customer shopping carts, like cutting power to the shop's filing cabinet.
EXP-002.expected: The cart service would gracefully fall back to local in-memory storage.
EXP-002.happened: Cart operations hung waiting for the datastore until our emergency brake stopped the test and restored it in 0.10 seconds.
EXP-002.means: This is a single point of failure: one datastore outage halts all carts. Fix: deploy Redis Sentinel replication and local LRU fallback.

EXP-003.did: We injected 500 ms of real kernel network delay into the suggestions service using a Linux netem sidecar, like a bad phone line.
EXP-003.expected: Slower suggestions, but the main storefront should still load briskly.
EXP-003.happened: The whole storefront page stalled to nearly 2,000 ms. Our emergency brake tripped and cleared the delay in 0.51 seconds.
EXP-003.means: A nice-to-have feature is slowing down critical page loads. Fix: wrap recommendation calls in non-blocking async promises with hedged timeouts.
